note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Teleconsult for new left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia for ~1 day in an adult woman on combined oral contraceptive; features most consistent with a first episode of migraine without aura; advised NSAID plus paracetamol, hydration, safety-netting, and BP check.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache since yesterday morning upon waking; left-sided, throbbing, fluctuates in intensity (never fully resolves), photophobia; prefers dark rooms.
- Timeline: Onset ~1 day ago; persistent with waxing/waning intensity; still “pretty bad” at time of consult.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Worse: Bright light/sunlight.
  - Better: Lying down; staying indoors/dark room.
  - Not worse: Bending forward; coughing/sneezing.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies visual changes, abnormal smells/tastes, nausea/vomiting.
  - Eating and drinking normally.
  - Denies feverish feeling (no temperature checked), skin changes/rash.
  - Denies focal neurologic symptoms (weakness, tingling, numbness).
  - No recent URI/cold symptoms; felt well the day prior.
- Gynecologic: Not linked to menstrual cycle; last period ~1 week ago.
- Prior headaches: No history of regular headaches or migraines.
- Function: Mostly at home; limited leaving the house due to symptoms.
- Context: Reports recent work stress.

Past Medical History:
- No significant medical problems reported.
- No recent hospital admissions or operations reported.

Medications:
- Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) — dose/route/frequency not documented; started ~6 years ago; no notable side effects reported.
- Paracetamol for current headache — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen) previously tolerated; not taken in the last few days.
- Allergies: Aspirin — causes nausea (intolerance; no anaphylaxis reported).

Social History:
- Lives with housemates/friends.
- Alcohol: A few drinks on weekends.
- Tobacco: Nonsmoker.
- Drugs: Denies illicit drug use.
- Occupation/stress: Reports recent work-related stress.

Family History:
- Mother: Hypertension; history of migraines.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not obtained (teleconsultation). Patient has not checked temperature but does not feel feverish.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consultation.
- Plan to arrange blood pressure check (per clinician advice).

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - New unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia, no focal deficits or systemic illness, most consistent with migraine without aura (first episode). Tension-type headache is possible but less likely given phenotype. Given estrogen-containing OCP use, CVST is a lower-likelihood but important consideration; no red flags elicited today.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Migraine without aura (most likely): Unilateral throbbing pain, photophobia, worsened by light, prefers rest/dark; family history of migraine supports. Opposes: No prior personal migraine history; no nausea/vomiting.
  - Tension-type headache (possible): Recent stress; improves with rest; lacks neuro/systemic signs. Opposes: Unilateral throbbing and photophobia more typical of migraine.
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (less likely but considered): OCP use and new headache. Opposes: No focal deficits/seizures; headache better lying down; very short duration; no other thrombosis risk factors mentioned.

- Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with photophobia — probable migraine without aura.
  - Plan:
    - Start an NSAID (e.g., ibuprofen) together with paracetamol as advised; ensure adequate hydration and rest in a dark/quiet environment. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Safety-netting: If not settling or worsening, if there is any change in the headache, development of fever/high temperature, or any rash, contact the clinic/seek care immediately (per clinician advice).
    - If headaches become persistent, recurrent, or menstrual-cycle related, schedule follow-up for further evaluation and management discussion.

- Issue 2: Blood pressure monitoring while on combined OCP.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange a blood pressure check (last reportedly normal ~6 months ago).
    - Obtain a home thermometer to monitor temperature if feeling unwell.

- Issue 3: Medication/allergy considerations.
  - Plan:
    - Avoid aspirin due to intolerance (nausea).
    - NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen) considered acceptable as previously tolerated; to be used alongside paracetamol as advised. Monitor for side effects.

- General plan items:
  - Return if any red flags develop (as above) or if symptoms fail to improve over the next 1–2 days.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: No vitals, neurologic exam, or objective physical exam recorded (teleconsult); temperature not measured; full medication list beyond contraception and current analgesics not reviewed; no pregnancy status recorded.
- Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear teleconsultation; some administrative details incomplete but clinical content intelligible.
